events.content:
The partial pre-rendering shell is now optimized. The route went from fully dynamic (shell = root layout + a generic spinner) to `◐ (Partial Prerender)`, with the static HTML shell containing the page heading, both stat cards, the revenue chart frame, and the invoices list frame as skeletons — verified in the built `index.html`. What was wrong: with `cacheComponents: true`, `page.tsx` awaited a single uncached `fetch` at the top of the page component. Since everything rendered after that await, nothing on the page could be pre-rendered — the entire route deferred to the `loading.tsx` spinner. What I changed: - **`app/page.tsx`** is now a synchronous component. The `

Dashboard

` and page structure render statically, and each section sits in its own `` boundary with a matching skeleton fallback, so sections stream in independently rather than all-or-nothing. - **`app/CardStats.tsx`, `app/RevenueChart.tsx`, `app/LatestInvoices.tsx`** became async server components that fetch their own data below their Suspense boundary, each exporting a skeleton that mirrors the real markup/class names to avoid layout shift when content streams in. - **`app/data.ts`** holds the shared `getDashboardData()`. The three components call it concurrently, but Next dedupes identical GET fetches per request, so it's still one upstream request — now non-blocking for the shell. `loading.tsx` is unchanged; it still covers full-route transitions, but first paint now comes from the deeper static shell instead. One option to consider: if the dashboard data tolerates staleness, adding `'use cache'` + `cacheLife` to `getDashboardData()` would bake the sections into the static shell entirely and revalidate in the background. I left it uncached on the assumption the data should be fresh per request.
